page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance type powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 372.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles four NVIDIA T4 GPUs from the Turing architecture family, delivering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1103.89 (bottom 25%) and a poor single-threaded gzip compression rate of 19.2 GB/sec (bottom 10%). Conversely, multi-core performance is strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 70574.45 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 287.37 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is also robust, featuring a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 3924.63 GB/sec (top 25%), though large-block uncached read and write speeds fall into the middle 50% average tier. Redis SET operations perform strongly at 64.27 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high resource density by combining a large physical core count with multiple enterprise GPUs, making it a viable option for parallelized workloads without the premium of top-tier flagship accelerators. However, the lack of local storage and the lower single-core performance are notable tradeoffs. The hardware profile and benchmark strengths make this instance suitable for multi-threaded workloads, GPU-accelerated machine learning inference, parallel data processing, Redis-based caching layers, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
